title: Diagram cardinality supplies an argument value to an adjacent whole
summary: GDT355 shows recurring eightfold and non-eight curved-lobe diagrams. A speculative Voynich functional hypothesis is that an independently counted diagram cardinality supplies an argument value to a nearby complete whole, while geometry itself remains reusable notation.

design.unit: complete diagram unit with independently counted compartments and adjacent complete whole
design.contrast: count is an input argument to the adjacent whole versus count is descriptive layout with no semantic input
design.prediction: Among repeated diagram units, changing the independently counted cardinality should change a predeclared argument/value slot while preserving the enclosure family; a fixed whole meaning predicts no count-conditioned slot change.
design.countermodel: The count may encode page organization or visual design only, and the adjacent whole may be a stable label unrelated to cardinality.
design.falsifier: Held units with independently observed counts show no count-conditioned slot change, or the same count feeds incompatible slots after controlling enclosure and panel role.
design.principal_risk: No current Voynich count-to-whole binding is independent; this is an exploratory functional hypothesis.
design.related: Near GDT354/GDT355 and JV cardinality draft, but tests cardinality as an argument input rather than fixed shape identity or phase roster.

source_evidence.quote:
- The exact narrow spiral-band rendering is a real local subseries: three
  adjacent pages, all with eight curved text-bearing compartments.
- The broader eight-curved-compartment family contains five pages after adding
  two decorated petal-like predecessors.
- Curved compartments are not an eight-value key. A nearby page has twelve
  curved, text-bearing lobes around a central circle.
- Four other surfaces have a clear eightfold primary division rendered as
  straight sectors or interlaced circles.
